pack.category: a new app for buying and selling used things with people nearby

ask.converted: How did your first sale or purchase go?
ask.using: What do you think of it so far?

pack.since: First sale or purchase on day {day}.

profile.does: A local resale app. Snap a photo of something you no longer use, set a price, and hand it over to someone nearby the same day.
profile.why: Things for sale close to you come first, so there is no shipping, no waiting and no long drive to pick up.

audience.who: People in US cities with a closet of things to sell, and people who would rather buy used and nearby than new.
audience.interests: Saving money, decluttering, buying second hand

money.paid: Buyers pay a 10% service fee on each purchase

ads.line: Free to list. Sellers keep every dollar.
Every buyer and seller is phone-verified.

competition.now: Big online marketplaces with shipping, and local listing boards full of strangers who never show up.
competition.switch: Reloop only shows things close enough to pick up today, from people with a verified phone.

retention.back: A note when something you saved drops in price or someone nearby lists what you looked for.
retention.leave: Nothing for sale nearby, or listings that sit for weeks with no buyer.

a.changes: Nationwide feed and search ads, everyone at once

b.changes: Seattle, then Portland on day 45; sellers first at local events, feed ads from day 14

meta.note: Simulated, calibrated to public benchmarks. Not observed.

verdict.headline: Plan B wins.
verdict.reason: Plan B stayed in Seattle and Portland and brought in sellers before buyers, so people found nearby things to buy. Plan A spread nationwide, leaving people with nobody close. Plan B won 30 of 30 runs.
